loop: Three results, three different next experiments — four outcomes in all. The branch taken is determined by the measured checks, not by the agent's preference, and every branch produces a revised dossier rather than a restated one. The agent writes the top box before it can see any of the numbers.
pipeline: The decomposition is fixed, not planned. The same five scouts run against the same sources for any target, so the only variable is the input. Each returns typed records rather than prose, which is what allows the harmonisation stage to operate on them mechanically instead of by re-reading summaries. Nothing reaches the harmonisation stage until its citation has been fetched and checked — see section 04.
concurrency: Measured from the reference run. All five scouts were dispatched in one message and ran concurrently, so 131 minutes of agent work finished in the 39 minutes taken by the slowest. Total cost was 1,086,955 tokens across 436 tool calls — the figure the dossier's own cost line will report.
target-landscape: Sortilin is data-poor but structurally viable. Against neurodegeneration comparators it sits two orders of magnitude below BACE1 on compound count, yet clears the only threshold that decides whether docking is possible at all. Cathepsin L (CTSL), the protease that processes progranulin, is the natural second target and is plotted for that reason. Counts are distinct compounds carrying a pChEMBL value, and PDB entries whose bound ligand exceeds 250 Da and 15 heavy atoms.
harmonise: Nothing here compares sources for a difference; every source contributes. Three kinds of sameness are resolved so that each fact is counted once: the same molecule across two databases, the same protein under several names, and the same evidence counted as records and as compounds. Receptor selection sits below the divider because it relates two different things — a patent series' core and a structure's bound ligand — and is therefore graded as an inference.
